 Kaohsiung turns purple ahead of BTS concert
 2026-11-13 
 Kaohsiung has gone completely purple for the first time! Ahead of BTS’ much-awaited concerts in Kaohsiung starting on Nov. 19, the city has pulled out all the stops to welcome them. From the harbor to the city’s landmarks, it seems that the color purple has erupted everywhere in honor of the K-pop band! Even the 85 Sky Tower has lit up for the first time for BTS. But it’s not just the city preparing to welcome them; legislators are doing their part too! Huang Chieh and Wu Pei-yi showed off their dance moves to one of the band’s songs. Kaohsiung seems to be buzzing in anticipation for the concert!
Global K-pop sensation, BTS is coming to town and Kaohsiung’s preparations for them are underway!
Chen Pei-hsin
FTV Reporters
To prepare for the arrival of BTS, Kaohsiung has lit the city and harbor up in purple, creating a warm welcome for ARMY all over the world. 
As the sun sets, Kaohsiung city glows purple in honor of BTS, who will soon take the stage!
Landmarks across the city are shining in mauve tones from The Dream Mall Ferris Wheel, Dragon and Tiger Pagodas, the Central Park Station Christmas tree to the dragon statue on Love River, and even 85 Sky Tower has lit up with a message for the band. 
ARMY member
Fan of BTS
It’s my first time seeing this, it’s quite special. 85 Sky Tower lit up for them too. We’ve waited too long and now they are finally coming to perform here! You can see how much heart the city has poured into this; I hope BTS will see it too!
ARMY member
Fan of BTS
What’s new is probably 85 Sky Tower, that’s the first time in history they have lit up, which is really iconic. It means all of Kaohsiung will glow more by these lights. 
Taiwan’s BTS craze is undeniable. Even legislators, Huang Chieh and Wu Pei-yi have joined in the fun by learning a complex dance routine in honor of their beloved band!
A purple storm has taken over Kaohsiung and it is forecasted to stay until BTS arrive in town on the 19!

 全市紫爆應援! BTS開唱倒數 高雄變身紫色港都
 2026-11-13 
 韓國天團BTS即將在11月19號，來高雄開唱，全城應援提前啟動。從港灣到市區，多處地標陸續點亮代表BTS的"’防彈紫"，就連85大樓也首度加入點燈行列。不只粉絲瘋狂，連立委黃捷跟吳沛憶，也用跳舞應援，紫色旋風已經席捲高雄。
韓國天團BTS即將降臨高雄開唱，演唱會還沒登場，城市應援已經搶先暖身。
[[民視新聞 陳姵妡]]
“為了迎接BTS到來，高雄從城市到港灣通通點上紫色燈光，要迎接全球的ARMY(BTS歌迷)到來。”
夜幕低垂，大港橋率先亮起紫色燈光，搭配港灣周邊地標，整片夜景彷彿披上紫色外衣。
還有夢時代摩天輪、蓮池潭龍虎塔，捷運中央公園的聖誕樹跟愛河畔的鰲躍龍翔的主燈，都加入點燈行列，就連85大樓也首度加入。
[[粉絲]]
“第一次看到覺得很特別。(85大樓)為了他活起來，就已經等他們很久，然後終於他們來這邊開演唱會，然後可以看到這個城市這麼用心在對待他們，希望他們也可以看到。”
[[粉絲]]
“新的(應援)應該是85大樓，那個是歷史以來第一次亮燈，所以是有蠻指標性，所以就等於說整個高雄，都會因為觀光而帶來很好的效益。”
BTS魅力無法擋，立委也加入追星行列，黃捷跟吳沛憶，合體挑戰BTS經典歌曲舞蹈，用舞蹈替偶像應援。
從城市點燈到各界接力應援，BTS還沒來台，高雄已經先颳起紫色旋風。

 Traffic backs up for 17km after truck plunges into drainage ditch
 A dramatic crash on Taiwan’s No. 1 Freeway brought traffic to a standstill on Friday afternoon, causing a massive 17-kilometer backup. A delivery truck was sent plunging through a guardrail and into a drainage ditch after colliding with a Mercedes-Benz sedan. The accident happened on the southbound lanes near the 38-kilometer mark. Fortunately, both drivers suffered only minor injuries. But recovering the truck proved particularly challenging, since the elevated Wuyang Expressway is directly overhead. Let’s hear more.
Chen An-hsu
Highway Police Bureau
The drivers of the two vehicles were taken to hospital with injuries. Both tested negative for alcohol. An investigation is underway to determine how the collision happened.
Operator
Transport company
If there is compensation to be paid, it’ll be paid. That goes without saying. The company will pay for all the losses.
Mr. Wang
Crane operator
The truck fell right under the southbound lanes of the elevated highway. If the boom becomes parallel to the ground, it’ll be difficult to lift it out. The boom should stay as upright as possible.
The 28-year-old Mercedes driver, surnamed Chang張, told police that his car suddenly lost power for unknown reasons. As he slowly moved toward the shoulder of the highway, his vehicle crashed with a delivery truck driven by a 48-year-old man surnamed Chen. The collision sent the truck crashing through the guardrail and down a forested slope and into a ditch. Both drivers remained conscious and were not found to have any severe injuries in the hospital. The transport company has also pledged to cover any resulting damages. The complex recovery operation, added to the disruption on an already congested stretch of highway near Linkou.

 Tainan’s new train station reports first 4-legged intruder
 A furry trespasser was caught wandering somewhere it definitely shouldn’t be at Tainan’s new railway station. A stray dog was spotted casually strolling along the tracks, giving passengers quite a laugh. But it also raised serious safety concerns. Staff and railway police rushed to track down the four-legged intruder, but the elusive dog remains on the loose.
A stray dog strolls along the train tracks just moments before a train is due to arrive, even stopping to relieve itself. This scene took place at Tainan’s new underground railway station, which has been open for less than a month. Passengers filmed the unexpected visitor and alerted station staff.
Member of public
Found dog funny
It was pretty funny, but also really dangerous.
Member of public
Wondering how dog got in
I have no idea how it managed to get in.
Member of public
Hoping for a piano concert
It made its way through that narrow gap. It was so cute! The train station has become so popular lately, maybe it’ll go play the piano!
Station staff teamed up with railway police and searched for the canine trespasser on the tracks. But with the vast space and complicated layout, their search came up empty. It is thought the stray dog made its way there from Daqiao Station, which is not yet fully underground.
Wu Wen-chieh
Tainan Railway Station Chief
It’s unlikely the dog came in through the station entrances, because our ticket gates are always staffed. We suspect it may have entered through the northern or southern approach ramps at either end of the tunnels.
While animals on railway tracks are not unheard of, underground sections pose a particular challenge. Being enclosed spaces, they make it harder for animals to find their way out, while also creating potential safety risks for passing trains. Tainan Station is now working with the local animal protection office to locate and capture the furry intruder. It will also step up patrols along the tracks and around station entrances to prevent another four-legged visitor from entering.

 16 middle schoolers get jabbed with wrong vaccine in Taitung
 More than a dozen students who were getting vaccinated, were administered the wrong shot in Taitung on Thursday. The 16 students were supposed to be receiving their flu shots, but instead got Covid vaccines. The local health bureau held a presser on Friday to apologize and explain the situation. But all that is known so far is that the wrong shots were delivered to the school, without concrete details on why that happened. The bureau says improvements will be made. Let’s hear more.
Chung Ming-hsia 
Taitung Public Health Bureau
We once again apologize for our mistake. We will conduct a thorough review to address the oversights, and we will do our best to improve. When the vaccination session was halted, we immediately informed the parents and the school. We will continue to monitor the kids’ health for the next six months.
Liu Fu-jung
Dawu Junior High School Principal
One student felt unwell after the vaccination and took leave. 
The bureau says the wrong vaccines must have been taken from the refrigerator they were initially stored in at the Dawu health center. The refrigerators there are clearly labeled, with different vaccines on different shelves, so it remains unknown why the mistake happened. The students were administered a Covid vaccine manufactured by Moderna, which is deemed safe for students aged 12 and up. Officials say verification procedures will be strengthened in the future.

 Trump sympathizes with Huang as Nvidia’s board appoint Kress
 If you think you are having a bad week, just know that Jensen Huang has it worse. The week began with him as rockstar CEO of one of the world’s largest tech companies and is ending with his title being stripped of him. After 33 years of running the company, it seems that a string of extramarital affairs have pushed him off the pedestal. CFO Colette Kress has stepped in as interim-CEO, she has been at Nvidia for 13 years and helped its revenue multiply 50 times. We are yet to see how the aftermath of this will shape Nvidia’s future and stability. 
Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang and his extramarital affairs have taken the world by storm, so much so that President Donald Trump has spoken out as well. 
Donald Trump
US President
The big thing is, was the woman a spy? And I don’t know if that’s been determined yet. But, if the woman was a spy, yes, if the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different. 
Just a month prior, Huang received the National Medal of Science at The White House by President Trump, who believes this extramarital affair has wrecked Huang’s career and was saddened to see it happen. 
Donald Trump
US President
I can tell you this; somehow he will end up on his feet. I mean, I know him, I know him pretty well. I always thought of him as a fine man and he is… I spoke to him yesterday, he is going through hell. 
Huang’s previous interview with Bloomberg seemed to be a self-fulfilling prophecy, it’s as if he knew then what was to come. 
Jensen Huang (Oct. 14)
Former Nvidia CEO
Just as I can be fired, the next CEO has to be hired. I like that we can’t be overly complacent about our position inside a company. And that we can’t take it for granted. And you’re always vulnerable. 
At the moment, it seems that Nvidia’s CFO, Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO. However, with Huang’s departure, it seems that Kress will have big shoes to fill.
Voice of financial expert
Reporting on Jensen Huang
He is a king maker of AI, and to lose the king creates a lot of instability. And so you know there’s going to be a big shift in the industry as well as Nvidia itself, it’s going to have to find a new leader, so you know it’s going to be hard. 
CNN Anchor
Reporting on Jensen Huang 
How do you replace someone of this caliber? 
Richard Quest 
CNN Business Editor-at-Large
You don’t. What you can hope is that you put in place, somebody who doesn’t do any harm or damage to the company? 
Huang had not designated a successor. This strategy has left the board scrambling to keep investor confidence and find a suitable person to carry the legacy forward. 
Richard Quest 
CNN Business Editor-at-Large
I think that’s a strategy that most people would disagree with, and has been found now to be wanting. 
Mohamed El-Arian
Economist 
This is a company with 40,000 people, talented. It has contracts; it has production growing, so it doesn’t get derailed immediately. 
Interim-CEO Kress has emphasized in a press release that Nvidia’s success is rooted in its talent and they will continue to build on the foundation laid by Huang. We are yet to see how the aftershocks of this week will affect the company’s global standing.

 Music teacher facing criminal charges for fake credentials
 An adjunct instructor who taught at an award-winning elementary school music program in Tainan for 13 years was recently reported on suspicion of forging a diploma from Taipei National University of the Arts. The school sent an inquiry to the university for clarification, and was told they have no record of the individual on file. When confronted later that day, the teacher admitted to forging the diploma and promptly resigned. Given that the deception lasted for over a decade, city education officials have ordered a comprehensive audit of the faculty and have filed a criminal forgery complaint with prosecutors. 
This elementary school music program in Tainan has many awards to its name, making its recent discovery of fraud all the more shocking. This university diploma looks genuine, but was found to have been forged by a teacher at the school.
School staffer
Discovered diploma fraud
We immediately called the registrar at Taipei National University of the Arts to verify it. After three days, they told us there was no student record under that name.
After receiving a tipoff in late September, the school contacted TNUA, which confirmed the diploma to be false. When confronted, the teacher confessed immediately and resigned. He said that since Taiwan at the time would not recognize his degree from China’s Xinghai Conservatory of Music in Guangzhou, he forged the credentials to get a job. Although he said he was willing to return all compensation, given his 13-year tenure, the city’s Bureau of Education intervened.
Chien Wen-ta
Tainan Bureau of Education official
We’ve ordered the school to conduct a comprehensive audit of hiring records, academic credentials, and hourly wage disbursements, and to retain all relevant evidence. As for the alleged document forgery, a criminal complaint has been filed with prosecutors. 
Colleagues who have worked alongside the teacher for years were shocked at the revelation, saying nothing about his teaching had ever raised suspicion. Parents were also in disbelief.
- We reviewed it.
- So you couldn’t tell that the diploma was fake? 
- No. It had a serial number, along with his ID number on top and his date of birth.
Voice of a student’s parent
Shocked at fraud revelation 
We only experienced his hard work and all his positive qualities. But since he told such a big lie, it ends up erasing all the good that came before it.
A single fake diploma sustained this deception for over a decade. In response, the school has initiated a comprehensive audit of faculty credentials and has retained legal counsel to determine all compensation disbursed to the teacher in preparation for a lawsuit. In the meantime, two teachers with verified master’s degrees have been brought in to take over the affected classes.

 ‘I worried you had a fever’ grabber unfazed when confronted by pharmacist
 An 87-year-old man is accused of making an unwanted move at a pharmacy in Miaoli, suddenly grabbing a female employee by both hands. The woman was left feeling extremely uncomfortable. But things took an even stranger turn the following day, when the two crossed paths on the street. She confronted him, demanding to know why he had grabbed her hands. He claimed he was simply checking whether she had a fever. The bizarre excuse left the woman furious, prompting her to call the police. Let’s hear more.
- Do you think that was OK? Grabbing my hand?
I was very uncomfortable.
- I can’t hold your hand?
- You grabbed my hands!
Who gave you the right?
You think that was OK?
- I worried you had a fever.
- Even if I did, there was no need to touch,
and in any case, you shouldn’t worry, I work at a pharmacy!
- Called the cops. He touched me!
He says he was right to touch me.
That it’s OK that he touched me.
He grabbed my hands.
Pharmacist
Was touched by elderly man
It was not OK. He regularly says things, like “I’ll miss you” and so on. I thought, whatever, I’ll just ignore him. But yesterday he actually touched me. If I let it slide, he would think it’s no biggie, and he might try to touch me somewhere else next time.
Ku Ching-wen
Police officer
Police officers intervened. After reviewing the footage provided, it was determined that Mr. Fan had taken advantage of a moment when the pharmacist wasn’t looking to grab her hands, which made her uncomfortable.
The pharmacist was so furious that she posted the footage online, warning others in the industry to be on their guard. She said the elderly man was a regular customer who had previously made inappropriate verbal advances. But this time, he crossed the line by actually putting his hands on her. Even afterward, the man appeared completely unfazed, saying he was almost 90 and that she could go to the police if she wanted. Police have since referred the case to the Miaoli District Prosecutors Office for investigation.

 Master calligrapher presents new and improved e-brush
 Master calligrapher Chang Bing-huang was recently invited to present the new “E-Brush Smart” app, created in collaboration between a tech company and Tamkang University. With just a tablet and a stylus, users can write soft-brush calligraphy featuring authentic artistic flourishes.
As part of traditional Lunar New Year celebrations, homes across Taiwan post couplets on their doors featuring large calligraphy. As fewer people are heading to the store for a brush and ink these days, maybe technology can fill in the gap.
After seeing him write the characters for Taiwan in freeflowing strokes, the skill of master calligrapher Chang Bing-huang is undeniable. The artist recently joined a tech company and the Carrie Chang Fine Arts Center at Tamkang University to present their new “E-Brush Calligraphy” app. With just a tablet and stylus, anyone can write stunning calligraphy in all five scripts. The participants had a chance to try it for themselves.
Since its introduction, the original digital e-brush has been exported around the globe to 45 different countries and regions. Sponsored by a semiconductor firm, Tamkang University teamed up with partners to upgrade the tool from an ordinary digital brush to a smart e-brush. The breakthrough overcomes the limitations of previous digital tools that failed to capture the look of traditional brushstrokes.
Chang Bing-huang
Calligrapher
I realized that if traditional calligraphy didn’t adapt, it would eventually be replaced by computers.
Chang himself helped design the app, with the demonstrations and brush previews all maintaining his personal style. The technology has also been used for the Fei-Yue documentary series produced by FTV. For 12 years, the series has explored Taiwan through aerial footage while documenting writers’ personal stories and works.
Chang Bing-huang
Calligrapher
For over 10 years, this important cultural program has showcased poets and literary works. Then I use my e-brush to write them out.
Chang has long contributed the title inscriptions and calligraphy for the program, not only enriching its cultural depth, but also enabling the art of calligraphy to keep spreading through broadcast media.

 Taiwan influencer scammed and threatened at Seoul cosmetics store
 A Taiwanese beauty influencer who goes by the social media name of Wang Hsun recently had a terrifying experience at a cosmetics store in Meyeong-dong District, which is Seoul’s premier business district. First he got hit with a massive NT$20,000 bill, then when he tried to get a refund, five or six people that included burly men surrounded him and pressured him to go into a small room at the back of the shop to talk it over in a way he found scary. While in the end he was able to get a refund, he was still coerced into spending over NT$3,000 on stuff he didn’t want. And after he complained to the Korean tourism authorities and made a video about his experiences, the store’s legal team threatened him and hackers tried to get inside his social media accounts. Let’s find out more. 
Taiwanese beauty influencer Wang Hsun was happily shopping in Meyeong-dong district in Seoul, South Korea, intending to buy some beauty and skincare products. However, he never imagined that stepping into a store would be the start of a nightmare.
Wang Hsun
Taiwan tourist in Korea 
As soon as I stepped out of the store, I checked my credit card record. It showed NT$20,000. I wanted to return the products, but they were incredibly scary. Suddenly, five or six people, including some burly men, surrounded me and said: “Why do you want a refund? Let’s go inside and talk.”They kept trying to lead me into a small room.
Although he eventually got a refund, Wang was forced to spend over NT$3,000 on unnecessary skincare products before he could leave. Afterwards, he complained to VisitKorea and even made a video of his experience back in Taiwan to warn other Taiwanese tourists. Unexpectedly, he received a threatening message.
Wang Hsun
Taiwan tourist in Korea 
The message basically said that they wanted me to take down the video, and that their company had a legal team that could prevent me from posting it. Many, many people said they encountered the same situation in the comments section of my video. Later, I actually received more than a dozen notifications that hackers were trying to enter my accounts, which has kept me up at night for the past few days.
If you’re just traveling abroad and don’t know anyone, what should you do to protect yourself if you encounter aggressive sales tactics?
943
Travel writer 
You should search for reviews online, or look out for Taiwanese people using coded terms to warn that a particular employee at a store might ring up extra items. After you pay, don’t just leave—double check your receipt against the items you actually received.
Wang originally went to Korea to buy beauty products, but instead of coming home with cosmetics, he left with a bellyful of infuriation.
